items.title: Can I get the CPU temperature and fan speed from the command line in OS X?
items.x_text:
❓ Can I get the CPU temperature and fan speed from the command line in OS X?

✅ Yes, use 'powermetrics' or Intel Power Gadget on macOS command line.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9v4icNxtdGc
#COSMOS #macos

discovery.short_answer: Yes, use 'powermetrics' or Intel Power Gadget on macOS command line.
discovery.full_answer: You can obtain CPU temperature and fan speed information on macOS using the command line utility 'powermetrics'. Running 'sudo powermetrics --samplers smc' provides various system metrics including CPU die temperature, which can be filtered using grep. For example, 'sudo powermetrics --samplers smc | grep -i CPU die temperature' shows the CPU temperature. Additionally, Intel provides the Intel Power Gadget, a tool that can be installed and launched to monitor CPU metrics including temperature and fan speed. These methods have been tested on macOS Mojave and provide reliable access to hardware monitoring data from the command line or via a graphical interface.
discovery.grok_perspective: Command-line retrieval of CPU temperature and fan speed on macOS can vary by hardware model and system version, with no guarantee of consistent or direct access across all setups.

youtube.title: How To Check Mac Temperature (Terminal Command + Free Stats App)

items.title: What can be done with bitter carrots?
items.x_text:
❓ What can be done with bitter carrots?

✅ Cook bitter carrots slowly with butter, salt, and a bit of sugar.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rHC8exWAgiE
#COSMOS #carrots

discovery.short_answer: Cook bitter carrots slowly with butter, salt, and a bit of sugar.
discovery.full_answer: To reduce bitterness and enhance sweetness in carrots, cook them slowly at low heat. A recommended method is to peel and cut the carrots into diagonal pieces about 2 cm thick, then cook them in a pan with butter, a small amount of sugar, salt, and black pepper. Cover the pan and cook for 25-35 minutes, shaking occasionally, until the carrots are tender but not overly soft. This slow cooking process helps bring out the natural sweetness and reduces bitterness. Additionally, using salt is more effective than sugar in minimizing bitterness, so add as much salt as possible without making the carrots too salty.
discovery.grok_perspective: Bitter taste in carrots may stem from growing conditions or storage, so confirming their safety and freshness before use is prudent.

youtube.title: The BEST way to cook carrots #chef

items.title: Are currency terms like USD, EUR, CNY used in all languages?
items.x_text:
❓ Are currency terms like USD, EUR, CNY used in all languages?

✅ Currency codes like USD, EUR, CNY are standardized but not universal in all languages.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CYf4pE61BaI
#COSMOS #terminology

discovery.short_answer: Currency codes like USD, EUR, CNY are standardized but not universal in all languages.
discovery.full_answer: Currency terms such as USD, EUR, and CNY come from the ISO 4217 standard, which provides internationally recognized currency codes. However, these codes are not necessarily used or known in all languages or regions. For example, in China, the ISO code CNY corresponds to the currency commonly called RMB locally. Similarly, Canada uses CAD as the ISO code, but locally it may be referred to as CDN. Different countries may have their own national standards that translate or adapt these ISO codes into local terms. For instance, China has a national standard GB/T 12406-2008 that lists Simplified Chinese names for ISO currencies, and Russia has its own standard ОКВ:2000. Therefore, while ISO currency codes are internationally standardized, their usage and recognition vary by language and locale.
discovery.grok_perspective: The adoption of codes like USD, EUR, or CNY may vary by regional practices and local conventions in different linguistic settings.

items.title: Can a white dwarf blow up by cooling down?
items.x_text:
❓ Can a white dwarf blow up by cooling down?

✅ No, white dwarfs do not blow up by cooling down.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=izpYIEK7ehA
#COSMOS #supernova

discovery.short_answer: No, white dwarfs do not blow up by cooling down.
discovery.full_answer: White dwarfs start very hot and cool over time, causing contraction and increased density. While theoretically cooling could raise density enough to trigger fusion and a supernova, typical white dwarfs formed through normal stellar evolution are not massive or dense enough to explode this way. The most massive white dwarfs are already very dense and degenerate, so cooling has little structural effect. In rare cases, more massive white dwarfs near instability might collapse into neutron stars rather than explode. Thus, cooling alone does not cause a white dwarf to blow up.
discovery.grok_perspective: Stellar remnants like white dwarfs follow complex evolutionary paths where cooling occurs gradually. Any link to explosive events would require examining additional physical conditions beyond temperature alone.

items.title: Is notifying X to Y actually used in modern English?
items.x_text:
❓ Is notifying X to Y actually used in modern English?

✅ Yes, but mainly in formal or official contexts, not everyday speech.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=n1WwRV9yxuo
#COSMOS #verbs

discovery.short_answer: Yes, but mainly in formal or official contexts, not everyday speech.
discovery.full_answer: The phrase 'notifying X to Y' is indeed used in modern English, though it is relatively rare and mostly found in formal or official contexts such as legal documents, government communications, and news reports. It appears more frequently in Indian English and British English sources, often in passive constructions like 'notified to the authorities.' While it is uncommon in everyday spoken English, it remains a valid and recognized expression in specific formal registers, especially when referring to the act of formally informing an authority or organization about something.
discovery.grok_perspective: Usage patterns for such phrasings can shift over time and vary by region or register, making broad claims about modern prevalence difficult without targeted data.

items.title: How can I improve a dehumidifier to floor drain interface?
items.x_text:
❓ How can I improve a dehumidifier to floor drain interface?

✅ Clean the drain, install a stainless grate, and secure hoses with ties.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hj1TCAD9rA8
#COSMOS #plumbing

discovery.short_answer: Clean the drain, install a stainless grate, and secure hoses with ties.
discovery.full_answer: To improve the interface between a dehumidifier and a floor drain, start by cleaning the drain area thoroughly, for example using a wire brush. Installing a new stainless steel grate can help protect and organize the drain opening. The condensate drain should maintain an air gap for safety reasons, so avoid altering that setup. To stabilize the drain components, use cable ties to secure the grate and the dehumidifier hose to the PVC piping. This setup helps prevent splashing and ensures the condensate flows smoothly into the drain, promoting effective drying.
discovery.grok_perspective: Modifying appliance-to-drain connections may introduce leak risks or drainage failures if not executed precisely. Professional assessment of the specific setup is recommended prior to changes.

items.title: What exactly constitutes an Oven Safe skillet or pan?
items.x_text:
❓ What exactly constitutes an Oven Safe skillet or pan?

✅ An oven-safe skillet can withstand high oven temperatures safely.

🎬 https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-FG14eZkC7o
#COSMOS #temperature

discovery.short_answer: An oven-safe skillet can withstand high oven temperatures safely.
discovery.full_answer: An oven-safe skillet or pan is designed to endure the high temperatures inside an oven without damage. Typically, these pans have solid metal handles because softer handle coatings cannot tolerate prolonged heat. Oven-safe pans can often withstand temperatures of 230°C (450°F) or higher, suitable for roasting or broiling. Materials like cast iron and stainless steel are commonly oven-safe and can handle even higher temperatures. Some nonstick ceramic-coated pans can tolerate temperatures over 300°C (600°F). Additionally, some pans include removable handle covers or silicone handle protectors to prevent burns when removing the pan from the oven. Choosing a pan with a comfortable, heat-resistant handle is important for safe and practical use in the oven.
discovery.grok_perspective: Oven safety for skillets or pans generally hinges on specific material tolerances and any temperature ratings supplied by the manufacturer, which can differ across items.
